name: Getting Hired and Getting Good
scope: Portfolio-over-resume, blog-as-career-lever, interview war stories, self-teaching paths

claims.claim_text: A candidate with little industrial experience can open an interview on hobby work by presenting a set of finished boards and inviting questions about them, which shifts the conversation from credentials to demonstrated work even when the projects themselves are simple.
claims.quote_verbatim: I don't have tons of experience, but I did really good work on these 10 boards I've already done. Here's my examples
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Layouts and Design-Outs

claims.claim_text: Dedicated external PCB layout houses hire only very fast, very capable designers working at the leading edge, so a practical route into layout is to take a general engineering job whose description includes layout, accumulate industrial board experience there, and only then apply to a layout-specific role.
claims.quote_verbatim: if they mention layout, go for that job, get some experience doing some industrial layout boards and then work from there
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Layouts and Design-Outs

claims.claim_text: Self-published project write-ups function as a supplement to a resume for early-career engineers: the resume states where a person has worked, while a public site shows what they actually built, and the site is worth presenting in a tidy, readable form.
claims.quote_verbatim: when you go to, if you're, you know, you're young and you want to get a job in the industry, point them to your blog site and make it look not fully professional, but at least make it look respectable
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Open Hardware and Self Publishing

claims.claim_text: Some hiring engineers explicitly prefer photographs of boards a candidate has designed over a submitted CV, on the grounds that the layout work itself carries information the credential summary does not.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can write me directly, but don't send me your resume. Send me pictures of boards you've designed
claims.speaker: Greg Charvat
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Dr Greg Charvat - Watcher of Wraithlike Walls

claims.claim_text: Bringing existing personal electronics work into an interview can displace the planned question set entirely, turning the meeting into a discussion of the candidate's own project; one engineer was hired into a first job this way without having intended to attend university.
claims.quote_verbatim: Went in for the interview. We got on like a house on fire. I showed them some of the electronics I was working on
claims.speaker: Andrew Seddon
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Andrew Seddon - Necessary Networked Novelty

claims.claim_text: Demonstrated work is the primary hiring currency inside the electronics industry: a candidate who can lay out boards and bring the resulting hardware to an interview can be hired largely independently of educational background.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you can demonstrate that you've laid out your own boards and you can actually bring along the hardware to the interview and go, look, I designed and built this
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Marcus Schappi - Kit Ketch Kenophobia

claims.claim_text: When a single opening draws dozens of student applications, grades carry little weight in the shortlisting decision; applicants with no side projects and no demonstrated outside interest are sorted to the bottom because other candidates have projects to show.
claims.quote_verbatim: I don't necessarily give a toss about your grades. It's what have you done
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Supply Chain Woes And Wares - Nonplussed Neotechnic Nithing

claims.claim_text: Arriving at an interview with work to show is a strong hiring lever, and an established public body of work under one's own name is stronger still, because the employer has already assessed the candidate before the interview begins.
claims.quote_verbatim: Going in with, to an interview with things to show is the best way to get a job by far. Even better than that is to already have your name established via a blogger, a YouTube channel or something like that
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with David Kronstein (Tesla500)

claims.claim_text: Interviewers of new graduates weigh hobby projects heavily and accept modest presentation formats such as a printed pamphlet or photographs; genuine engagement with the project is readable during the discussion, and simulated enthusiasm is also readable.
claims.quote_verbatim: Definitely hobby interests are really good. I mean, if they show me a project they've done, sometimes people bring a little pamphlet in or pictures of their project
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Art Kay

claims.claim_text: Fixing a piece of broken equipment belonging to an interviewer during the interview itself can be decisive, because it demonstrates applicable skill in the employer's own environment rather than describing it.
claims.quote_verbatim: I think I passed the interview when I fixed a test bed for one of the people who was interviewing me
claims.speaker: Nash Reilly
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Nash Reilly

claims.claim_text: A self-imposed project deadline forces a learner through material they would otherwise skip — for example teaching themselves Linux kernel module development to finish an animation project — and the resulting story of what was learned and how supplies concrete interview material.
claims.quote_verbatim: he rolled up his sleeves and taught himself how to do all this stuff. I mean, that kid's going to get hired real fast
claims.episode_title: Embedded Linux with Jay Carlson

claims.claim_text: Board-level design skill does not transfer to integrated-circuit design: a competent practical electronics designer faces a difficulty gap of orders of magnitude in moving to chip design, and no amount of reading books and designing boards substitutes for it.
claims.quote_verbatim: you prove, can you do it? So you bring your stuff along to your job interview
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Firmware, Netburner and Semiconductors - Chris's Capitalism Colloquy

claims.claim_text: A resume's only function is to secure an interview; hiring decisions are not made from it. Generic top-ten resume advice is written for mass-market filtering, so a candidate deliberately targeting employers who value distinctiveness can reasonably ignore it.
claims.quote_verbatim: the sole goal of a resume is to get you in for the interview. That's it. People don't hire based on the resume
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: SpaceX, Enclosures & Startups - Urging Unemployment Ullagone

claims.claim_text: A resume can be written neutrally to serve many applications, but where a specific employer requirement is known — a particular microcontroller family, for instance — the resume should be reordered so that experience is the focus rather than merely present. Recruitment agents push for this reordering because their commission depends on the placement.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're really after... If you know that they're after something very key... Right. ...you should always modify your resume to highlight
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: SpaceX, Enclosures & Startups - Urging Unemployment Ullagone

claims.claim_text: Listing high school or elementary school on an engineering resume adds nothing and reads poorly; a chronological work history starting from the end of formal education already discloses approximate age regardless.
claims.quote_verbatim: another bad thing to put on there, folks, is your high school and primary school
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: SpaceX, Enclosures & Startups - Urging Unemployment Ullagone

claims.claim_text: After graduation the degree and institution move to the bottom of the resume and the operative question becomes whether the candidate can do the work, which is tested through questions and through the projects they present.
claims.quote_verbatim: which courses, you know, you did in which university that goes to the very bottom of your resume. Nobody cares. It's like, it's like, can you do the job
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Drab Olive

claims.claim_text: A student building a product for themselves can name that effort as a small company and list it under work experience rather than as a hobby, which places the same substance in the section a resume reader weights most heavily without misstating what was done.
claims.quote_verbatim: I think it's better to make up a name for your company and then say you're building it for your company and then listed under work experience
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Drab Olive

claims.claim_text: Industry resumes and academic CVs invert each other: industry places work experience first and qualifications and publications last, while academia counts papers, patents, grant income and student numbers at the top.
claims.quote_verbatim: in practical engineering jobs, you know, your qualifications almost don't matter. So, like, they go down the bottom of your resume, your publications go down the bottom, and your work experience is everything
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jonathan Ellis

claims.claim_text: Personal projects belong on the resume with working links to where they are documented, not omitted as unprofessional; a candidate who already publishes project videos in their chosen speciality is already distinguished from the overwhelming majority of graduates.
claims.quote_verbatim: where are all your projects? Like, he's like, Oh, I don't think I should put those on. I'm like, no, you should definitely, definitely put those on there. And, and links, links to your website
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Living Through Chipageddon

claims.claim_text: Engineering resumes are conventionally held to one or two sheets, and a single sheet for a young candidate.
claims.quote_verbatim: we always recommend, I'm sure both of us will recommend keeping your resume to like one or two sheets tops
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Living Through Chipageddon

claims.claim_text: Including photographs of built hardware in a resume works against reviewer fatigue: a reader flicking through a hundred documents registers a visually distinct one and remembers the candidate, which materially raises the chance of an interview.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's okay if you include a whole bunch of photos, because trust me, when you've got a hundred resumes and you're flicking through them
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Living Through Chipageddon

claims.claim_text: Where resume space forces a choice, a technical project line outperforms unrelated service-job experience of the kind careers offices recommend as evidence of work ethic. Candidates without projects can start by taking an existing open-source project, modifying it and documenting the change.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you have to choose between putting another project line on your resume and your Dairy Queen experience, put the project line
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Living Through Chipageddon

claims.claim_text: Even employers that publicly downplay formal qualifications still route applications through a human-resources screen, so a candidate must satisfy the stated checklist first and only then compete on the substance an engineer reading the resume will care about.
claims.quote_verbatim: you still have to get through HR. Right. So you've got to have whatever they're looking for
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Living Through Chipageddon

claims.claim_text: Most resume readers give a document only seconds of attention, which makes a well-prepared application more valuable than interview-day presentation choices such as wearing a suit, since a resume can eliminate a candidate outright while dress code only applies once the interview has been won.
claims.quote_verbatim: You have, like, three seconds, maybe, with most readers of resumes
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Prepping For Hoverboards - Gallionic GitHub Gabble

claims.claim_text: Resume screening is routinely delegated to a working engineer who receives a stack of a hundred applications alongside their normal duties, which is the structural reason candidates do not receive individually considered readings.
claims.quote_verbatim: At jobs I've worked at, I have gotten a hundred resumes to look through. They slam it on my desk. It's like half a foot high
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Prepping For Hoverboards - Gallionic GitHub Gabble

claims.claim_text: Spelling and presentation errors do not sink an obviously ideal candidate, but they decide between borderline candidates competing for a fixed number of interview slots, so their cost is concentrated at the margin where most applicants sit.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you've got a crappy-looking resume and somebody else who I might give the same, you know, have the same inkling for, then I'm sorry, but you're going to miss out
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Prepping For Hoverboards - Gallionic GitHub Gabble

claims.claim_text: A useful division of interview preparation is to normalise on the conventional signals — dress, spelling, formatting — so that no attention is spent defending them, and to differentiate on technical work; clearing the conventional checkboxes and then showing a strong project covers most of the distance to an offer.
claims.quote_verbatim: certain things you want to normalize on, certain things you want to stand out from the pack
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Prepping For Hoverboards - Gallionic GitHub Gabble

claims.claim_text: Employers retain the resumes of unsuccessful applicants and return to that pool first when a later opening appears, so an unsuccessful application can still produce a future contact.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've kept their resumes because you know I might need somebody else for something
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Jobs For Weirdos

claims.claim_text: A single publicised engineering job advertisement can draw on the order of five hundred applications, setting the scale against which any individual resume competes.
claims.quote_verbatim: Last time I put up a job ad, I got like 500 resumes
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Augmented Engineering

claims.claim_text: Automated application filters reject candidates on mechanical grounds unrelated to fit: a candidate a company had explicitly said it wanted to talk to was auto-rejected for missing a checkbox in an online application system, with no notification of why.
claims.quote_verbatim: because of a filter system on LinkedIn, he didn't click the right button and he just got immediately rejected
claims.speaker: Dave Young
claims.episode_title: Rebuilding Projects with Dave Young

claims.claim_text: A common rule of thumb holds that a role held under twelve months is better omitted than listed, because the hiring company reads short tenure as a problem; the counter-practice is to keep the entry and, if asked in interview, state plainly what was wrong and what the candidate would do differently.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you stayed a job less than 12 months, well, you know, there's a, you know, there's a kind of rule of thumb that says, well, you probably shouldn't put that on your resume because it looks bad
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Google Glass, Lean Startup and VotC - Initializing Instructed Interviews

claims.claim_text: Two to three years per employer reads as a sound resume pattern while repeated stays under a year reads badly, and since roughly nine in ten startups fail, an exciting new-company role can end well before that window is reached.
claims.quote_verbatim: two or three years looks decent on your resume. We've talked about this many times before. You know, it looks decent. Anything less than a year
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Gotta Update My Dog

claims.claim_text: Hiring for a multi-year project makes tenure pattern decision-relevant: a resume showing consistent two-year moves signals to the hiring manager that the candidate is unlikely to stay for a five-year programme.
claims.quote_verbatim: if I look at a resume and they've moved every two years, then I know that's pretty consistent pattern
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Augmented Engineering

claims.claim_text: One interviewing method deliberately keeps technical questions very easy and escalates only if the candidate answers, because struggling on simple material is itself the discriminating signal.
claims.quote_verbatim: My interview questions are really easy at the job. I deliberately keep them incredibly easy
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Fremescent Floccose Fortification

claims.claim_text: A single elementary circuits question such as asking a candidate to analyse a voltage divider is estimated to eliminate around thirty percent or more of applicants for electronics roles, and proportionally more for co-op and intern positions.
claims.quote_verbatim: what's a voltage divider, right? Or give them a voltage divider question. It's like, man, that'll take out 30
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Google Glass, Lean Startup and VotC - Initializing Instructed Interviews

claims.claim_text: Lateral-thinking puzzle questions copied from large software employers carry no relevance to electronics work; they presuppose that candidate filtering has already happened elsewhere and are aimed at ranking an already-screened pool.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've been to a couple of job interviews where they try and copy that Google technique of asking these men's type, you know, the high IQ club. They're like these puzzle questions
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: LED Designs, Last Minute Designs and Board Designs

claims.claim_text: Taking a candidate into the lab and working through a measurement together forms part of some technical interviews, testing investigative method rather than recall.
claims.quote_verbatim: So I go into the lab. I've asked that too, I mean. You know? Yeah. Yeah. Cool. And we start measuring things, and we start investigating it, you know, and that's part of the job interview
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Bonkers Birthday Badinage

claims.claim_text: Large employers hiring at volume may decide on psychometric or team-exercise results rather than technical assessment; one two-hour psychometric exam produced an unsolicited offer of a management role the candidate had neither applied for nor wanted.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've been to job interviews, yeah, where I've had the psych exam and they would come back after
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Supply Chain Woes And Wares - Nonplussed Neotechnic Nithing

claims.claim_text: Making a public portfolio a hard hiring requirement excludes candidates whose work is confidential, contractually restricted or simply private; a better procedure is to interview on other signals and then ask the candidate to show work privately.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you make anything like that a requirement, right? Like just saying, just like saying you need to have a PhD in order to get this job
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: CAD courses and cross platform creation - Printing Propaedeutic Patterns

claims.claim_text: Disclosing an outside technical blog or channel during interviews doubles as a test of the employer: a company that asks a candidate to stop publishing, or whose staff resent colleagues spending outside time on technical work, has revealed a culture problem before the candidate accepts.
claims.quote_verbatim: I talked to a couple companies, and one of them said, yeah, we don't want you to do that anymore
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Hardware, Surveys and Giveaways - Radular Rental Ranting

claims.claim_text: Outside publishing can be fatal late in a hiring process even after every technical interviewer approves: at one secretive company the technical rounds were all passed and the senior non-technical decision-maker objected on the basis of the candidate's public activity alone.
claims.quote_verbatim: he just looks at my resume and goes and shakes his head
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Hardware, Surveys and Giveaways - Radular Rental Ranting

claims.claim_text: Sustained hackerspace membership stated on an application functions as a strong hiring signal for some interviewers, because regular attendance evidences continuous hands-on practice outside paid work.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'm a member of a, you know, I'm a senior member of a hackerspace and I'm there, you know, five times a week
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ben Krasnow - Sprauncy Saccadic Spintherism

claims.claim_text: Attending interviews without wanting the role is used deliberately as maintenance: it keeps a practitioner current on what employers expect candidates to know and on how interviews are being conducted.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'm always looking for a job just for fun. Sometimes just for kicks, you know, to find out what a company's like
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Catalyzing Change Agents

claims.claim_text: Interviewing is a skill that engineers are not taught in the first decade after graduation, on either side of the table; instructional material for it is more often framed from the interviewer's perspective — how to ask — than the candidate's.
claims.quote_verbatim: the first five, 10 years of getting out of school, interviewing is an area that you just don't learn
claims.speaker: Elecia White
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Elecia White - Wirewove Worshipping Wookieist?

claims.claim_text: Asking a prospective employer whether it has ever failed to make payroll is a diagnostic question for a candidate assessing a small company, with a single occurrence carrying different weight from a repeated pattern even when each is explained.
claims.quote_verbatim: have you never not been able to make payroll? I think that's actually a really great question to ask in an interview
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Gremlins in the machine

claims.claim_text: Approaching known contacts inside a target company can fail entirely when the candidate is remote and cannot hold attention in person; in one case an application only progressed once it reached, by accident, someone with an actual need, who then conducted an hour-long international telephone interview.
claims.quote_verbatim: a guy phoned me up and he interviewed me on the phone for about an hour
claims.speaker: Philip Frieden
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Philip Freidin - Xenodochial Xilinx Ex-Employee

claims.claim_text: Interviews arranged speculatively through recruiters at companies with no advertised opening can still produce offers, because a hiring engineer who finds a candidate capable may create the position; entering a company as a technician is also a viable foot in the door, since internal staff hear of openings before they are advertised.
claims.quote_verbatim: the recruitment consultant had no idea if they had any jobs going, but they said, oh, look, they're, they're always looking for people
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: What defines an engineer? - Job Judging Jeremiad

claims.claim_text: Publicly visible prior work compresses the hiring process: when an opening appeared suddenly at a module vendor, the candidate's already-reviewed public projects allowed a notably short interview process for a field applications role.
claims.quote_verbatim: they'd actually, and they told me this during the interview process, which itself was remarkably short as a matter of fact
claims.speaker: Jeff Roberg
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeff Rowberg - Mini Module Master

claims.claim_text: A specific, known-difficult, practical university course can act as a hiring differentiator on its own, because passing it while engaged with the material carries information about the candidate that a grade average does not.
claims.quote_verbatim: You take that class. You pass it. And I hear from someone that you were struggling and enjoyed it. I'll hire you in a second
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Melbourne, Hackerspace & Calibration - Vacuuous Vortex Verification

claims.claim_text: Technical audiences accumulate slowly rather than arriving at launch; one channel that eventually reached around five thousand regular viewers began with an upload watched by roughly ten people, and persistence over time was the operative variable.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you're a new blogger out there and you start up, you know, you've just got to stick to it. You've just got to work at it. And, uh, cause audiences don't just come
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: What's In A Name?

claims.claim_text: Publishing tutorials while learning, rather than after mastery, builds credibility precisely because it exposes the learning process and helps readers at the same stage; this route can establish an electronics reputation for someone whose formal study is in an unrelated field.
claims.quote_verbatim: he started a site and he started doing tutorials as he went along, you know, and, and that's given him credibility. It shows his learning process
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: China, Entrepreneurs and Blue Collar Reality

claims.claim_text: A deliberate practice of posting short work-in-progress notes on every working day, published where professional contacts read them, is used to make an engineer's output continuously visible rather than visible only at job-change time.
claims.quote_verbatim: he advised to blog about your job every single day or regularly at least to show people what you are doing
claims.episode_title: Freelance PCB Design with Petr Dvorak

claims.claim_text: A published book operates as an unusually heavy professional credential — handed over as a record of what the author did — and carries more weight in commercial settings than an equivalent body of online writing.
claims.quote_verbatim: books as like the biggest business card you'll ever hold
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jon Oxer - Innoxious Implant Innovator

claims.claim_text: A staged transition from salaried engineering to full-time video production took roughly four to five years: viewer-funding plus platform revenue first reached about half of prior income, prompting a move to part-time employment, with full salary replacement following around six months later.
claims.quote_verbatim: it took a long time, maybe, maybe four years until I realized. And after four or five years, Patreon actually was coming out
claims.speaker: Mehdi Sadaghdar
claims.episode_title: Electroboom!

claims.claim_text: Relocating to a lower-cost city can create the runway for going independent: a mortgage a little over five hundred dollars a month, combined with an existing subscriber base, was sufficient to leave a salaried hardware role and work full time on an open-source machine.
claims.quote_verbatim: I had bought a house in Pittsburgh and I quit my job
claims.speaker: Stephen Hawes
claims.episode_title: A Benchtop Pick and Place with Stephen Hawes

claims.claim_text: Part-time technical writing taken on to supplement income from an unrelated profession can become the primary career: writing alongside orchestral work and private teaching converted to a full-time role when the publication was acquired in 2013.
claims.quote_verbatim: I started, you know, writing part-time for Hackaday as a way to kind of round out my income
claims.speaker: Mike Szczys
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Mike Szczys

claims.claim_text: Academic journal publication and hobbyist-magazine publication signal differently to an industry resume reader: peer-reviewed papers carry little weight in practical hiring, while articles in practitioner magazines register as relevant demonstrated work, because the editorial process and the audience differ.
claims.quote_verbatim: if I'm reading someone's resume and it says, oh, I've published these papers, and they're like, hey, I'm going to go, I don't give a shit
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Magnets, China & IEEE - Xenomorphic Xerox Xebec

claims.claim_text: Professional-society membership is cheap for students and accrues a visible membership duration; a new graduate showing ten years of membership signals early orientation to the professional ecosystem, and a lapsed membership resets that count.
claims.quote_verbatim: it shows up once you graduate how many years you've been an IEEE member
claims.speaker: Shahriar Shahramian
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Shahriar from The Signal Path - Quisquous Quivering Quadripole

claims.claim_text: For an experienced tradesperson entering electronics design without a degree, the practical route is a portfolio plus a first paid foothold — a short contract or a troubleshooting engagement — which then becomes the first resume entry and generates referrals.
claims.quote_verbatim: I mean, I think one is portfolio. We've talked about that a lot
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Call In Show #3

claims.claim_text: Self-description on a resume matters for a self-taught entrant: someone doing design work should describe themselves by the work rather than by a prior trade label, provided the claim can be substantiated, and noting that in some jurisdictions the title engineer is legally regulated so electronics designer is the safer term.
claims.quote_verbatim: you should be calling yourself an electronics engineer or an electronics design engineer
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Call In Show #3

claims.claim_text: Self-selection out of applying is a common failure among self-taught candidates; the working expectation is that a persistent applicant with hobby-built projects to show will absorb many rejections before finding the employer who values that work.
claims.quote_verbatim: A lot of people – the problem with a lot of people is that they don't actually go for these engineering jobs. They think, oh, I'm not going to get it
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Call In Show #3

claims.claim_text: The Art of Electronics functions poorly as a first textbook but effectively as a refresher: a few weeks of concentrated reading was enough for an engineer returning after time away from design work to re-enter interviews prepared.
claims.quote_verbatim: That's how I recapped all of my knowledge and got hired for a job. It was like, I was out of design for a while. I just started reading Art of Electronics for like a couple weeks straight
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: FPGA, Xess, 32 Bit - Quirky Qualitative Questions

claims.claim_text: Deliberate replication is an effective self-teaching loop: retype or rebuild a known-good example, compile or test it, locate the divergence, and correct it. The method supplies well-defined failure points that can be searched or asked about, and it builds procedural fluency rather than recognition.
claims.quote_verbatim: look at a textbook maybe, or look at a video, like one of Dave's videos, replicate it, see what you did wrong, and then go back
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: FPGA, Xess, 32 Bit - Quirky Qualitative Questions

claims.claim_text: Prior hobby experience makes formal study more effective: scattered practical knowledge acquired beforehand is uncohesive on its own but locks into place when the underlying theory is taught, and it supplies the motivation to care about the material.
claims.quote_verbatim: that's the advantage of having the hobby background in engineering before you actually go to formally learn it
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: FPGA, Xess, 32 Bit - Quirky Qualitative Questions

claims.claim_text: Abstract concepts such as real-time operating system primitives are best approached from a concrete problem rather than from a book read cold; without a use case for the material to attach to, the concepts generally fail to stick outside a sustained student mindset.
claims.quote_verbatim: you need to scratch an actual itch. Like you shouldn't try and learn the concepts just out of the blue
claims.speaker: Benjamin Cabe
claims.episode_title: Benjamin Cabé Nose Zephyr

claims.claim_text: Some roles erode capability rather than build it, and because employability tracks current skills, tenure at such a position steadily reduces the holder's options elsewhere; the point at which learning stops is a practical trigger to move.
claims.quote_verbatim: you look around and you realize that, that, that people lose skills over time at some jobs as compared to gain them. And then you realize the longer you work there, the less employable you are anywhere else
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Adam Wolf - Brick & Board Biuners

claims.claim_text: Online technical courses lack recognised certification, which motivated attempts at formal micro-credentials; an alternative assessment used in hardware teaching is that a working board constitutes the pass, and the board itself is then portable evidence at an interview.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you build the board and it works, that's ultimately your pass or fail. Like, I don't care how you got there. And you can take that along to your job interview
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Tesla, Checklists and Bullies - Emerging External Eupsychics

claims.claim_text: Hiring managers reportedly weigh a named course taken through an online platform equally with the same course taken in a classroom when scanning a resume; either serves to secure the interview rather than the job.
claims.quote_verbatim: when a hiring company, a hiring manager looks at a resume, looking at what courses have they taken, either at school or at a MOOC, they're equally important
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Eric Bogatin - Tilded Thumb Tenets

claims.claim_text: Identity verification is the principal limitation on online-course certification: platforms cannot confirm that the account holder sat the assessment, which is why some university programmes require on-site presence for at least some exams.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's always the question of is this person that has signed in with this account, is that the person that took the exam
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Eric Bogatin - Tilded Thumb Tenets

claims.claim_text: A repair-training model rests on the observation that low-value, high-nuisance repair work is uneconomic for degreed engineers commanding six-figure salaries, so transferring a fraction of that knowledge to someone outside the field opens a viable middle income; documented outcomes include a former food-service worker starting an electronics recycling business.
claims.quote_verbatim: if I can teach somebody one-fifth of what the engineer knows, will that person be able to do the job for one-fifth of that engineer's salary
claims.speaker: Louis Rossmann
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Louis Rossmann

claims.claim_text: At one fabrication lab, beginners who took introductory classes almost never returned for the open project sessions where they could have applied the material; the observed flow ran the other way, with people attending open project sessions first and taking classes afterwards.
claims.quote_verbatim: The overlap between the classes and the open house events actually ran the opposite direction. People would show up to the open house events and then go to the classes
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Finishing Prototypes with Zack Freedman

claims.claim_text: The characteristic blocking state for a self-teaching beginner is not lacking an answer but lacking the vocabulary to search for one, and this state is hard for experienced practitioners to reconstruct — a reason to keep deliberately learning unfamiliar subjects.
claims.quote_verbatim: that feeling of just like, man, I just don't know where to turn next. I don't know what to Google for
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer
claims.episode_title: Keyzermas Vacation

claims.claim_text: Sign languages may lack established vocabulary for electronics components and concepts, so a deaf learner faces a barrier deeper than not knowing what to search for: the shared terms needed to frame the question do not exist in the language.
claims.quote_verbatim: There just aren't words in that language. Right. So like. When they developed ASL. Why would they have words about resistors
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Once Every Couple Months

claims.claim_text: Basic electromagnetic compatibility — mental models of how current moves rather than test-lab procedure or memorised standards — is identified as the highest-value self-directed study area for a young PCB designer, and one that many universities cover poorly.
claims.quote_verbatim: I think the first big one is EMC
claims.speaker: Zachariah Peterson
claims.episode_title: Layout Review with Zachariah Peterson

claims.claim_text: Component and tool vendors have expanded free engineer-education material over roughly the past decade because their customer base depends on newly trained users, which has steadily increased the resources available to self-teaching designers.
claims.quote_verbatim: the corporate world has been doing a great job over the past approximately a decade of stepping up and realizing that if they want to have a customer base for their products, they need to do new customer education
claims.speaker: Zachariah Peterson
claims.episode_title: Layout Review with Zachariah Peterson

claims.claim_text: Front-loading engineering programmes with calculus and physics is associated with roughly fifty percent attrition across the first two years.
claims.quote_verbatim: you go in engineering programs and they stick you in calculus, they stick you in physics
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Shifting Away From DIY - Pedetentious PnP Progress

claims.claim_text: A teaching assistant's observation across several years of introductory transistor and op-amp courses is that mathematically inclined students find the first two years easy while students with a hands-on background often struggle and drop out; students also differ in whether they absorb an explanation as an intuition or require the equations written out.
claims.quote_verbatim: the mathematics types, they have a very easy first two years in uni. And the people who were, you know, soldering the back of TVs when they were 12, they have it quite hard and they quite often drop out
claims.episode_title: High End Audio with Remco Stoutjesdijk

claims.claim_text: Where a degree programme is heavily theoretical, working in industry during study — placements at large firms and startups alongside coursework — is one route to the practical exposure the curriculum omits, and to sustaining motivation.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'd have to get out of my way to go and work for a company. For example, I worked at Intel. I worked for some startups and I worked at Fujitsu all while studying
claims.speaker: Shrouk El Attar
claims.episode_title: Creative Engineering with Shrouk El-Attar

claims.claim_text: Immigration status can bar entry to engineering education outright: an asylum seeker in the United Kingdom was excluded for about six years, a restriction subsequently lifted at more than seventy-five universities following an organised access campaign.
claims.quote_verbatim: being an asylum seeker meant that I couldn't access engineering for many, many, many years, for about six years
claims.speaker: Shrouk El Attar
claims.episode_title: Creative Engineering with Shrouk El-Attar

claims.claim_text: A one-credit seminar covering consumer and patient safety — regulatory process, hipot versus ESD testing, grounding rationale — occupies about an hour of lecture and two hours of outside work per week, and covers material absent from conventional undergraduate curricula.
claims.quote_verbatim: How you go through the regulatory process. What it means to do a high pot test versus a ESD test
claims.speaker: Eric Van Wyk
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Eric VanWyk - Meiotic Mountenance Mooshimeter

claims.claim_text: One engineering grading scheme assigns marks by number of successive prototypes iterated, on the reasoning that demonstrated progress through revisions — not a single trivially altered version — is the thing being assessed.
claims.quote_verbatim: you do one prototype, you get a D. You do two prototypes, you get a C. You do three prototypes, you get a B
claims.speaker: Clint Cole
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Clint Cole of Digilent

claims.claim_text: An engineer returning to a university in 1997 after years in industry found the curriculum — topics, designs, textbooks — unchanged since their own studies, illustrating how slowly engineering course content tracks industrial practice.
claims.quote_verbatim: I came back to WSU, Washington State University, to see if I wanted to be a full-time academic
claims.speaker: Clint Cole
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Clint Cole of Digilent

claims.claim_text: Choice of teaching EDA tool affects graduate employability: a free chip-design flow lacks process design kits for smaller nodes and is not used industrially, so students taught on it are less marketable than those taught the commercial tool employers actually run.
claims.quote_verbatim: someone that's trying to educate students and make them marketable and attractive to potential employers is they don't use electric in industry. They use Cadence
claims.speaker: Jake Baker
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jake Baker

claims.claim_text: Industry-taught classes differ from professor-taught ones by narrowing from broad theory to one concrete application of it, and by using CAD tools; since engineering in practice is executed through those tools rather than by hand analysis, understanding how a tool processes information and what it assumes is itself part of the subject.
claims.quote_verbatim: when you have somebody from industry teach a class, uh, they hone in on the way that the, they use that theory
claims.speaker: Brock Lameres
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Brock LaMeres

claims.claim_text: An argument for plural entry routes into engineering holds that the discipline is defined by taking knowledge from science and building and maintaining systems that benefit society, which vocational training, two-year degrees and one-year certificates can all support; the objective is more kinds of engineer, not a single lowered standard.
claims.quote_verbatim: not everybody needs a PhD in electrical engineering to become an engineer
claims.speaker: Brock Lameres
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Brock LaMeres

claims.claim_text: Frequent low-stakes assignments serve an early-warning function as much as an assessment one: daily deadline data reveals which students are disengaging, allowing individual outreach before failure, in contrast to a two-large-exams model that surfaces problems only after the fact.
claims.quote_verbatim: These homework assignments are basically, they take maybe five minutes and they're just to show that they did watch the video
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Brock LaMeres

claims.claim_text: A semiconductor company staffs system-level roles substantially by hiring practitioners out of the applications side of the industry and by seating people with basic skills alongside those with practical experience; the underlying view is that formal education teaches how to learn, with the practical content acquired after the degree.
claims.quote_verbatim: what I learned in school, uh, just taught me how to, how to learn when I got out in the industry
claims.speaker: Hank Zumbahlen
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Hank Zumbahlen - Zoppa Zumbahlen Zateticism

claims.claim_text: One teaching stance holds that students should build durable intellectual scaffolding and identify the invariants that survive technology change, rather than learn the tactics of getting today's design done; the counter-argument is that this reasoning is also used to avoid updating course material, and that a hands-on component using something at least approximately modern is what makes the abstractions usable later.
claims.quote_verbatim: Think about building your intellectual scaffolding so that you can put other things on top of it as technology inevitably changes
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Tom Lee

claims.claim_text: Formal study supplies the model of why hardware is built the way it is — which constraints produced which structures, and which new constraints those structures introduced — while the specific quantitative constraints, such as a three-cycle budget on an L1 cache, are learned on the job while building the thing.
claims.quote_verbatim: you build the foundations through school. You model your brain
claims.speaker: Julia Desmazes
claims.episode_title: Chip Design for Fun (and Waffles) with Julia Desmazes

claims.claim_text: Building and publishing engineering projects does not correlate with academic performance in the same discipline; the gap between solving exam problems and working on real designs persists, and outside project fluency is not evidence of classroom aptitude nor the reverse.
claims.quote_verbatim: school won't teach you everything that you need to know to like build things practically
claims.speaker: Aaed Musa
claims.episode_title: Robots Everywhere with Aaed Musa

claims.claim_text: Teaching a subject is an effective way to master it: a graduate student who had performed poorly in an undergraduate computer architecture course knew the material thoroughly after taking a semester away from research to lecture it.
claims.quote_verbatim: I didn't do really well in the course when I was an undergrad and I took it. But I knew it backwards and forwards by the time I finished teaching it
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Vic Aprea - Federated Firmware Functionalism

claims.claim_text: Career norms differ by region: in several Asian markets engineering is structured as a stepping stone to management, so remaining a practising engineer after a decade is read as failure — a constraint on how long a technical track can be sustained in those markets.
claims.quote_verbatim: in many of the Asian countries like Malaysia, Singapore, even in China in some ways, if you're an engineer in 10 years, you're a failure. Engineering is a step to management
claims.speaker: Jack Ganssle
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jack Ganssle - Embedded Elchee Epexegesis

claims.claim_text: A senior engineer in the United States earns a six-figure salary against a national median family income of about fifty-one thousand dollars for all earners combined; Australian engineering salaries reach six figures locally but a six-figure design engineer there is doing comparatively well.
claims.quote_verbatim: once you become a senior engineer, you're making a six-figure salary. That's the average family income in this country for the whole family
claims.speaker: Jack Ganssle
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jack Ganssle - Embedded Elchee Epexegesis

claims.claim_text: The standard advice for an engineer who dislikes their speciality is to change jobs directly rather than enrol in further study first, on the reasoning that additional coursework does not itself open the target field.
claims.quote_verbatim: if I go and study this other course, will that give me an avenue to get out? Well, no, not really. Just get out and go and get another job
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: China, Entrepreneurs and Blue Collar Reality

claims.claim_text: Early career direction is strongly path-dependent: the internship or co-op determines the first specialisation, that specialisation is what appears on the resume, and subsequent applications are naturally directed at similar work, compounding the initial choice.
claims.quote_verbatim: you start with an internship or a co-op, right? I mean, that defined a lot of my stuff
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: PCBs, Tektronix & Ham Radio - Habitual Handicraft Hangups

claims.claim_text: An internship is worth taking when it yields a discussable project, substantive experience, or work alongside a strong practitioner; a placement spent on repetitive production-line work provides none of these and adds little beyond the resume line.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you only had three months to do an internship and you could like get some kind of project out of it that you could talk about in your next interview
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Timing is Everything

claims.claim_text: Technical support functions as a recognised internal route into engineering roles at some electronics companies because support work demands deep product knowledge; the side effect is that the support organisation continually loses its strongest hires to engineering.
claims.quote_verbatim: It seems like you guys said that a lot of you came from tech support. Is that kind of the normal process at SparkFun
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with the SparkFun Team - Efficacious Engineering Ensemble

claims.claim_text: Large companies are easier to enter early in a career and harder later: an experienced candidate is more expensive, understands the organisation's methods and is less compliant, which reduces their attractiveness for entry-level hiring.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's probably easier as a young person to get hired into a big company right now
claims.speaker: Bob Davidson
claims.episode_title: Impedance Matching" with Davidson and Vandenbout - Presbytes Pushing Portfolios

claims.claim_text: An engineering career built without a degree can be established by accumulating a reputation as the person to approach for a given kind of design work; that reputation then carries the holder through toy design, chip design, corporate research labs and founding companies.
claims.quote_verbatim: I started coming to Silicon Valley and started doing engineering without any college degree. So I just brute forced my way into startup life
claims.speaker: Jeri Ellsworth
claims.episode_title: Jeri Ellsworth and the demise of CastAR

claims.claim_text: Adding a scarce adjacent skill can convert hobby competence into paid work: discrete-logic and RF projects attracted no interest, but the ability to program a microcontroller in assembly produced paid odd jobs and, via a contact met at a hobbyist meetup, an on-the-spot hire at a toy company for someone whose degree was in English.
claims.quote_verbatim: people did care all of a sudden once I could program an assembly
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Todd Bailey - Embedded Embrasure Engineering

claims.claim_text: One model for staying technically engaged over a long career is to treat each new domain as a self-directed programme of roughly four to five years, reusing the method of learning acquired during doctoral work; documented iterations covered chip design, optics and electronics manufacturing in sequence.
claims.quote_verbatim: I like to say my life is a series of PhDs, but I don't actually go to school to get them
claims.speaker: Bunnie Huang
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Bunnie Huang (2nd)

claims.claim_text: Anticipated stagnation is used as a departure trigger independent of dissatisfaction: an engineer left a role because staying longer was expected to erode the habit of learning, with family and relocation factors reinforcing rather than causing the decision.
claims.quote_verbatim: I felt like I'm not going to grow. And I felt like if I stay longer, I may become the lazy person
claims.speaker: Robert Feranec
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Robert Feranec

claims.claim_text: Vendor certifications during the information-technology boom commanded very large salaries and drew career switchers in volume; when the market collapsed those switchers found the credential would not secure even a fraction of the former pay, illustrating the risk of retraining into a single credentialled boom market.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you got one of those, right, you were guaranteed a $200,000 a year job at the time
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Hardware, Surveys and Giveaways - Radular Rental Ranting

claims.claim_text: Consulting is not an entry-level path: hired consultants have almost invariably accumulated employed experience first, and experience of both large and small organisations broadens the capability a consultant later sells.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you look at any consultant that anyone has ever really hired, they didn't do that out of college. They've gone and earned their stripes somewhere
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Siloed Engineering with Leigh Brady

claims.claim_text: Regional electrical and firmware engineering communities are small enough that former colleagues recur across employers within a single career, which makes departures on bad terms a durable liability.
claims.quote_verbatim: you don't want to burn any bridges in this area because you're going to run across the same people that you met earlier on in life
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ken Burns

claims.claim_text: Reputation inside a company is set early and cheaply: having a solution already prepared when a task is assigned produces an outsized impression, and a single such instance can establish a standing that persists for the rest of a tenure there.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you're starting your new engineering job, that's the way to do it. Building that stuff to make you look like a hero
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Distribution, Wozniak & Robots - Early Eight-bit Endgame

claims.claim_text: Founding leadership and continued technical practice are largely exclusive: taking charge of a hardware company means spending the time on fundraising rather than on engineering.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you want to keep being an engineer, you don't get to go hunting for money. If you want to be in charge, you've got to go hunt for the money
claims.speaker: Ahmed
claims.episode_title: Standing With Ahmed

claims.claim_text: A graduate degree may function as an admission filter rather than a capability requirement in engineering, where a bachelor's degree suffices for most work; the contrast is with sciences such as neuroscience or biology, where a doctorate is needed even to be considered.
claims.quote_verbatim: I think I could do the work without the degree completely, but, uh, whether or not I would be considered in this pool of applicants with other people, I have no idea
claims.episode_title: Grad School Time Capsule with Joshua and Zach

claims.claim_text: Campus job fairs collect thousands of student resumes of which only a fraction of a percent progress, though some employers do attend with intent to hire on the spot in double-digit numbers.
claims.quote_verbatim: they get thousands of resumes from interested, you know, college students. But, you know, that only a fraction of a percent of those actually get anywhere
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer
claims.episode_title: DJ and Jazzy Jeff

claims.claim_text: Semiconductor vendors supply free parts for university final-year projects as a recruiting channel, tying the offer to academically credited work so that students give it the six months of effort a credit-bearing final project receives.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're doing a final project, write to TI, we'll give you a bunch of free chips, and then we'll try and hire you afterwards
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: DIP projects, OSHW & Trade Booths - Demonstrative DIP Dacrygelosis
